derivations.claim: Finite evaluation. On each projector $e(i)$ the dots are commuting nilpotents by [F1]. If $y_r^{n_r}=0$, every monomial of total degree greater than $\sum_r(n_r-1)$ vanishes. Thus formal series have finite evaluation, and $c+f$ with $c\ne0$ and $f$ of positive degree has inverse $c^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-f/c)^k$. Unequal-colour spectral differences have nonzero scalar constant; equal-colour dot differences will only be used as formal divided differences, never inverted in the cyclotomic algebra. [F1, algebra]

A faithful formal calculation convention. Temporarily take independent dots $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ and a separate copy of their fraction field for each colour word. Let $S_r$ swap both positions and their dots; write multiplication on the right of $S_r$. For spectral variables $A,B$, put $\widehat p=(A-B)^{-1}$ in DG and $\widehat P=(1-q)B/(B-A)$ in NG, even on equal colours. The affine Hecke operator is $H_r=S_r(1-\widehat p)-\widehat p$ in DG and $H_r=S_r(1-\widehat P)-\widehat P$ in NG. For precision the formal calculation algebra has coefficients $\bigoplus_i F[\![u_1,\ldots,u_d]\!]e(i)$ and the affine generators, with spectral word-sliding: an unequal-colour intertwiner moves $e(i)$ to $e(s_ri)$ and permutes coefficients, while on equal colours the affine mixed relation gives its divided-difference correction. These relations follow in a sector by the CRT projectors and the mixed presentation: multiply the unequal spectral difference by the intertwiner and use its unit inverse; on equal colours use $H+1$. This calculation is faithful before any cyclotomic quotient: move coefficients right by these mixed and word-sliding relations and reduce crossing words by the Coxeter relations to span the finitely many $H_we(i)$; in their crossed-product expansions the coefficient at a reduced permutation $w$ is a product of nonzero rational functions and every proper subword has smaller length. A maximal-length coefficient therefore proves independence, also for formal series coefficients after clearing their finitely many difference denominators. Consequently an identity between regular formal expressions can be checked in this rational model and then evaluated at nilpotent dots. This is a calculation in the affine presentation, not an assumption that its cyclotomic quotient acts faithfully. [F2, algebra]

Explicit normalization. Write $u=y_r,v=y_{r+1}$, $p=(i_r-i_{r+1}+u-v)^{-1}$ on unequal DG colours, and $A=q^{i_r}(1-u),B=q^{i_{r+1}}(1-v)$ on NG colours. In the order equal, unrelated, forward arrow, backward arrow, double edge, choose $q_r(i)$ to be $1+v-u$, $1-p$, $(1-p^2)/(v-u)$, $1$, $(1-p)/(v-u)$, respectively, and choose $Q_r(i)$ to be $1-q+qv-u$, $(A-qB)/(A-B)$, $(A-qB)/(A-B)^2$, $q^{i_r}$, $q^{i_r}/(A-B)$, respectively. These are the actual five branches, including $e=2$. For DG forward colours $i_r-i_{r+1}=-1$, so $1-p^2=(v-u)(2-u+v)/(1-u+v)^2$; on the double edge the field has characteristic two and $1-p=(v-u)/(1+u-v)$. Thus the forward quotient has constant $2
e0$ unless the pair is a double edge, which uses the separate constant $1$ branch. Unrelated pairs have $i_r-i_{r+1}
e0,\pm1$, so $1-p$ has nonzero constant. In NG the unequal $A-B$ is a unit; $A-qB$ has nonzero constant except for a backward arrow, whose coefficient is prescribed separately. Hence all five coefficients are units; the equal coefficient has constant $1$ in DG and $1-q
e0$ in NG. [step 1.1, algebra]

The full affine coefficient check. In left-coefficient notation $H_{AB}=a_{AB}S+b_{AB}$, use $(h,t)=(1,0)$ in DG and $(q,q-1)$ in NG, where $b_{AB}=-(A-B)^{-1}$ or $(1-q)B/(A-B)$, respectively, and $a_{AB}=h-b_{AB}$. Direct common-denominator multiplication gives $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$, $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$, and $b_{AB}b_{BC}=b_{AC}(b_{AB}+b_{BC}-t)$. The mixed relations follow by multiplying $A,B$ on either side; the first two identities give $H^2=tH+h$. For three positions, expansion of either braid word has coefficients, in the order $1,S_1,S_2,S_1S_2,S_2S_1,S_1S_2S_1$, equal to $b_{AC}(h+b_{AB}b_{BC})$, $a_{AB}b_{BC}b_{AC}$, $a_{BC}b_{AB}b_{AC}$, $a_{AB}a_{AC}b_{BC}$, $a_{BC}a_{AC}b_{AB}$, $a_{AB}a_{AC}a_{BC}$. For example the first expansion's constant is $b_{AB}^2b_{BC}+a_{AB}a_{BA}b_{AC}$, which reduces to the displayed constant using the three scalar identities. The $S_1$ coefficient reduces from $a_{AB}(b_{AC}b_{BA}+b_{AB}b_{BC})$ in the same way. Thus this six-coefficient check establishes braid for all spectral triples, including any coincidence of colour labels; spectral variables remain independent at this stage. Disjoint positions commute. [step 1.2, algebra]

Pair products and interchange. Denote the chosen normalizer by $N_{ij}(u,v)$, the piecewise scalar by $p$ in DG or $P=(1-q)B/(B-A)$ in NG, and put $K_{ij}(u,v)=1,v-u,u-v,(v-u)(u-v)$ in the four unequal-colour cases. Substitution gives $p_{ij}+p_{ji}(v,u)=0$ in DG and $P_{ij}+P_{ji}(v,u)=1-q$ in NG. Also $N_{ij}(u,v)N_{ji}(v,u)K_{ij}(u,v)=1-p_{ij}^2$ in DG and $(1-P_{ij})(q+P_{ij})$ in NG. For the latter equality, its right side is $(B-qA)(A-qB)/((B-A)(A-B))$; forward and backward pairs use $B-qA=q^{i_{r+1}}(u-v)$ and $A-qB=q^{i_r}(v-u)$, respectively, and a double edge uses both. These substitutions prove each branch of the pair-product identities without division by a nonunit. Each coefficient depends only on its ordered two colours and their two dots. Therefore swapping a third position gives the same coefficient of the same ordered pair, proving the three-position interchange identities for $p,P,N$. In particular no square root is chosen. [step 2.1, algebra]

The intertwiners. On unequal colours $\varphi=S(1-p)$ and $\Phi=S(1-P)$, since the scalar term cancels. Hence they permute the word and the two spectral variables, their squares are the pair products in step 3.1, and they commute at distant positions. On equal colours they are $H+1$; their squares are $2\varphi$ and $(1+q)\Phi$. The equal-colour mixed correction is $1+B-A$ in DG and $qB-A$ in NG, obtained by multiplying the operator $H+1$ by $B$ and subtracting $A(H+1)$. The braid defect is zero unless the outer colours coincide. For all equal colours, expanding $(H_1+1)(H_2+1)(H_1+1)$ minus its reversed word gives $h(\varphi_1-\varphi_2)$ in DG and $q(\Phi_1-\Phi_2)$ in NG (here $h=1$ in DG). For outer equal, middle unequal, write $C_{AB}=1-\widehat p_{AB}$ or $1-\widehat P_{AB}$, and $F_{AB}=C_{AB}C_{BA}$. The middle equal-colour intertwiner contributes either its permutation term or its scalar term $C_{AC}$. The former gives equal longest-permutation coefficients in the two words; the latter gives identity coefficients $F_{AB}C_{AC}$ and $F_{BC}C_{AC}$. Their difference is therefore $C_{AC}(F_{AB}-F_{BC})$. In DG put $p_1=1/(A-B),p_2=1/(B-C)$ and use $p_1+p_2=(A-C)p_1p_2$; then this difference is $(p_1-p_2)(p_1p_2-p_1-p_2)$. In NG, substituting $C_{AC}=(A-qC)/(A-C)$ and $F_{AB}=(A-qB)(B-qA)/(-(A-B)^2)$ cancels the factor $A-C$ and gives $(1-q)^2(AC-B^2)(AB-qBC)/((A-B)^2(B-C)^2)$. Adjacent-equal and distinct-colour patterns have no remaining identity term; their permutation coefficients cancel by the scalar identities of step 2.2. These are precisely the intertwiner identities named in the Statement. [step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

A local crossing calculation that will also serve both relation maps. Put $D_r f=(S_rf-f)/(u_r-u_{r+1})$; every inverse dot difference in an operator formula acts by multiplication on the left unless explicitly included in a right coefficient. On equal colours, $H+1=(S+1)(-N/(u-v))$, since $1-\widehat p=-N/(u-v)$ in DG and $1-\widehat P=-N/(u-v)$ in NG; thus $(H+1)N^{-1}=D$. On unequal colours set $c_{ij}(u,v)=(1-p)/N_{ij}$ or $(1-P)/N_{ij}$, so the normalized crossing is $S_rc_{ij}$ and $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$ by step 3.1. For a formal coefficient $f$, direct subtraction gives $Df=(Sf)D+(Sf-f)/(u-v)$ and $D^2=0$; unequal crossings simply permute coefficients. These formulas prove the dot-sliding and quadratic relations and the compatibility $\psi_r^2N_r(i)S_rN_r(s_ri)=1-p_r(i)^2$ or $(1-P_r(i))(q+P_r(i))$ on unequal colours; on equal colours both sides of the original compatibility identity are zero. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

Every braid colour pattern. Write $u,v,w$ for the three dots, $W=S_1S_2S_1$, and $c=c_{ik}$. If all colours are distinct, both crossing braid words have right coefficient $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$ at $W$. For $(i,i,k)$ both are $(W-S_1S_2)c(u,w)c(v,w)/(v-w)$; the coefficient product is symmetric in $u,v$, so moving it through $D_1$ adds no divided-difference correction. For $(i,k,k)$ both are $(W-S_2S_1)c(u,v)c(u,w)/(u-v)$, by the same calculation with the product symmetric in $v,w$. In these two formulas the denominator multiplies on the left and the coefficient product multiplies on the right. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest-permutation terms cancel by the ordered-pair interchange of step 3.1; the remaining identity coefficients in $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1$ and $\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$ are $-K_{ij}(u,v)/(u-w)$ and $-K_{ij}(w,v)/(u-w)$. Thus their difference is $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)$, equal to $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$ for unrelated, forward, backward, double-edge pairs. Finally all equal colours give $D_1D_2D_1=D_2D_1D_2=-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. Each displayed quotient is a formal divided difference; the resulting braid correction is polynomial, including characteristic two. This proves all five cases locally. [step 5.1, algebra]

Regular identities and conclusion. The rational calculations above express every intertwiner, normalization, dot-sliding, quadratic and braid identity as an identity of regular formal expressions in the affine generators. Faithfulness in step 1.2 licenses clearing the temporary differences, and step 1.1 licenses finite evaluation in the sector. The candidate normalizers and their products give all stated identities, retaining $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}y_r(i)$ in NG. Therefore all three assertions of the Statement hold over the original field, with no algebraic closure or choice principle. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 6.1] ∎

derivations.claim: A faithful KLR calculation, before quotient. Use independent dots and the rational operators of the normalization supplier’s local crossing and braid calculations: equal crossings act by $D=(S-1)/(u-v)$ and unequal crossings by $Sc_{ij}$, where $c_{ij}=(1-p)/N_{ij}$ in DG or $(1-P)/N_{ij}$ in NG. The pair product is exactly $K_{ij}$ and the five braid computations give corrections $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$, with the specified braid order. Thus these operators satisfy the affine sign-modified KLR presentation. This representation is faithful for formal dot coefficients: moving dots right by the proved sliding rule, use quadratic relations to remove repeated simple reflections and braid relations to reduce each crossing word to a chosen reduced word plus shorter words. This terminates by length (and the finite Coxeter reduction at each fixed length), giving a spanning family $\psi_we(i)$. Its leading permutation coefficient is a product of nonzero $c_{ij}$ and of $1/(u-v)$ for equal pairs; proper subwords have smaller permutation length. Maximal-length comparison in the matrix crossed product therefore proves independence of the formal coefficients. Clearing finitely many temporary dot differences is legitimate in this faithful affine calculation. It does not assert faithfulness after taking the cyclotomic quotient. [F1, F2, algebra]

The mixed and quadratic computations. In the representation of step 1.1, the displayed inverse Hecke element $\psi N-p$ (DG) or $\psi N-P$ (NG) is literally $S(1-\widehat p)-\widehat p$ or $S(1-\widehat P)-\widehat P$ on every word. On unequal colours this follows by cancellation of the right coefficient $N$; on equal colours $\psi=D$ and $D N-1=H$ by the equality $H+1=(S+1)(-N/(u-v))$. The supplier’s full affine coefficient check gives the mixed relation $Hx_{r+1}-x_rH=1$ in DG, and $HX_rH=qX_{r+1}$ in NG, together with $H^2=1$ or $H^2=(q-1)H+q$. Alternatively the DG mixed constant on an unequal word is $(i_r-i_{r+1}+u-v)p=1$, and on an equal word it is $(u-v)+N=1$; in NG the same spectral substitution gives the stated mixed identity. Commuting dots, distant mixed relations and distant crossings follow because the operators involve disjoint pairs. By step 1.1 these are regular affine-KLR identities and hence evaluate in the nilpotent-dot quotient. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

All five Hecke braid patterns. For a triple with distinct colours, adjacent repeated colours $(i,i,k)$ or $(i,k,k)$, outer repeated colours $(i,j,i)$, or all equal colours, the inverse elements of step 2.1 have precisely the same rational Hecke operator $H$ on each successive word. Their two braid products therefore have the six coefficients listed in the supplier’s full affine coefficient check; this table applies to each of the five patterns because spectral variables, rather than colour constants, are used in its denominators. The required scalar reductions are $b_{AB}+b_{BA}=t$, $a_{AB}a_{BA}=h+tb_{AB}-b_{AB}^2$, and $b_{AB}b_{BC}=b_{AC}(b_{AB}+b_{BC}-t)$, with $(h,t)=(1,0)$ or $(q,q-1)$. In the outer-repeated pattern the KLR braid correction $u+w-2v$ on a double edge was already included in the faithful model of step 1.1, so it is not suppressed by this table. In the equal pattern $D$ accounts for all divided-difference terms. Equality of the six explicit coefficients, followed by faithfulness, proves Hecke braid inside the formal KLR algebra; its regular expressions descend to the cyclotomic quotient. This proves the missing four cases and the all-equal case without assuming any Hecke intertwiner relation in that algebra. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

The cyclotomic relation and the homomorphism. The cyclotomic relation $\prod_i(x_1-i)^{\lambda_i}=0$ (respectively $\prod_i(X_1-q^i)^{\lambda_i}=0$) holds because $y_1^{(\Lambda,\alpha_{i_1})}e(i)=0$ is the cyclotomic KLR relation and $x_1=\sum_i(y_1+i_1)e(i)$ (respectively $X_1=\sum_iq^{i_1}(1-y_1)e(i)$) is a shift of the dot. Hence all defining relations of the affine cyclotomic quotient are satisfied, and the universal property of the presentation gives a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_d\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ carrying the generators to the displayed elements. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

Identification of $\sigma(e(i))$. By [F2] the algebra $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite-dimensional, so it becomes a finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_d$-module through $\sigma$. The simultaneous generalized weight space for $\sigma(x_r)e(i)=(y_r+i_r)e(i)$ in DG, or $\sigma(X_r)e(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i)$ in NG, on $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is exactly $e(i)R^\Lambda_\alpha$ when $i\in I_\alpha$ and is $0$ otherwise, by the nilpotence of the dots and the weight relation. Hence $\sigma(e(i))$, being the projector onto that generalized weight space for the commuting operators $\sigma(x_1),\dots,\sigma(x_d)$ in DG, or $\sigma(X_1),\dots,\sigma(X_d)$ in NG, equals $e(i)$ for $i\in I_\alpha$ and vanishes otherwise. [F2, step 4.1]

Factorization through the sector. Since $e_\alpha$ is central and $\sum_ eta e_ eta=1$ in $H^\Lambda_d$ ([[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]]), and since $\sigma$ annihilates all idempotents $e(i)$ with $i
otin I_\alpha$ by step 5.1, the element $\sigma(1-e_\alpha)=0$. Therefore $\sigma$ kills $e_ eta$ for $ eta
e\alpha$ and every corner $e_ eta H^\Lambda_de_\gamma$ with $( eta,\gamma)
e(\alpha,\alpha)$, and it factors through the central summand $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_de_\alpha$ as a unital homomorphism. [step 5.1, algebra]

Conclusion. Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 produce the homomorphism $\sigma$ from the verified affine and cyclotomic relations; steps 5.1 and 6.1 identify its action on the content idempotents and show that it kills all other sector corners, restricting to a unital homomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$. No choice principle is used. [step 4.1, step 6.1] ∎

derivations.claim: The cyclotomic and dot-sliding relations. The first KLR relation follows from the cyclotomic relation [F2] and the invertibility of $(x_1-i_1)$ respectively $(1-q^{-i_1}X_1)$ off the summand $e(i)$: on $e(i)$ the dot $y_1$ is nilpotent and $x_1=y_1+i_1$ respectively $X_1=q^{i_1}(1-y_1)$, so $y_1^{(\Lambda,\alpha_{i_1})}e(i)=0$ accompanies the cyclotomic relation. The dot and idempotent relations are immediate from the definitions of the idempotents $e(i)$ and the dots $y_r$, and the dot-sliding relations follow from the dot-sliding intertwiner identities, the definitions of $p_r(i),P_r(i)$ and the equal-colour case of the normalization. [F1, F2, algebra]

Quadratic and all braid patterns. Work first in the faithful formal affine-Hecke calculation of the normalization supplier, then evaluate its regular identities in the sector. On equal colours the normalized intertwiner is $D=(S-1)/(u-v)$, so $D^2=0$ and $Dv-uD=1=vD-Du$. On unequal colours it is $Sc_{ij}(u,v)$, with $c=(1-p)/N$ in DG or $(1-P)/N$ in NG; its square is $c_{ij}(u,v)c_{ji}(v,u)=K_{ij}(u,v)$, giving respectively $1,v-u,u-v,(v-u)(u-v)$. For the braid, put $W=S_1S_2S_1$ and dots $u,v,w$. Distinct colours give both words $Wc_{ij}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{jk}(v,w)$. For $(i,i,k)$ both words are $(W-S_1S_2)c_{ik}(u,w)c_{ik}(v,w)/(v-w)$; for $(i,k,k)$ they are $(W-S_2S_1)c_{ik}(u,v)c_{ik}(u,w)/(u-v)$, with denominators on the left and coefficient products on the right. The products are symmetric in the two equal-colour variables, so their divided differences vanish. For $(i,j,i)$ the longest terms cancel and the identity coefficients differ by $(K_{ij}(w,v)-K_{ij}(u,v))/(u-w)$; direct substitution gives $0,1,-1,u+w-2v$. On all equal colours the common value is $-(1-S_1-S_2+S_1S_2+S_2S_1-W)/((u-v)(u-w)(v-w))$. These are the supplier's explicit local computations, using only affine-Hecke relations and scalar normalizers, not the opposite relation-map lemma. The double-edge correction and its sign remain valid in characteristic two. Clearing temporary differences in the faithful formal calculation gives regular relations; only those relations, and unit coefficients, are evaluated on nilpotent dots. Hence every quadratic and braid relation (1.14)–(1.15) holds in $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. [F1, F2, algebra]

The homomorphism. The verified relations are exactly the presentation of $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ recalled in [F2] and in [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], so the universal property of that presentation gives a unique $F$-algebra homomorphism $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ sending the generators to the displayed elements. No choice principle is used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct]

Conclusion. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 verify all relations of the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR presentation for $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$, and step 2.1 invokes the universal property to produce $\rho$. The zero sector is included: all constructions are supported on the projectors $e(i)$, which may vanish. [step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

derivations.claim: The forward composite on dots and crossings. On each KLR word the map $\sigma$ kills all idempotents outside content $\alpha$; in particular, since the inverse polynomial generators of $R$ have exactly the eigenword projectors $e(\nu)$ (the nilpotent dots shift distinct scalar eigenvalues), $\sigma(e_\alpha)=1_R$ and $\sigma$ annihilates every other central sector. The composite $\sigma\rho$ fixes $y_r$ by [F2], and on a crossing $\sigma\bigl(\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}e(i)\bigr) =\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)+P_r(i)\bigr)Q_r(i)^{-1}e(i)=\psi_re(i),$ using the definitions of the local generating elements in [[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]]; the degenerate case is the same computation with $\varphi_r,p_r,q_r$ in place of $\Phi_r,P_r,Q_r$. These are literal ordered expressions, not a commutation of $\psi_r$ with its coefficient. Hence $\sigma\rho$ fixes every presentation generator of $R^\Lambda_\alpha$. [F1, F2, algebra]

The reverse composite on generators. By [F2] the composite $\rho\sigma$ fixes the idempotents and dots; on a word, $\rho\bigl(\psi_rQ_r(i)-P_r(i)\bigr)e(i) =\Phi_rQ_r(i)^{-1}Q_r(i)e(i)-P_r(i)e(i) =T_re(i)$ in the nondegenerate case, and the same with $s_r$ in the degenerate case. Again the evaluation is a finite expression in the nilpotent variables. For the polynomial generators the computations are $\rho\sigma(x_re_\alpha)=\sum_i((x_r-i_r)+i_r)e(i)=x_re_\alpha$ in DG and $\rho\sigma(X_re_\alpha)=\sum_iq^{i_r}(1-(1-q^{-i_r}X_r))e(i)=X_re_\alpha$ in NG; their inverses are fixed because homomorphisms preserve inverses. Conversely $\sigma\rho(y_re(i))=(\sigma(x_r)-i_r)e(i)=y_re(i)$ in DG and $(1-q^{-i_r}\sigma(X_r))e(i)=y_re(i)$ in NG. Along with the projector identities of [F1], these verify every presentation generator of both algebras, including the correct inverse NG substitution. Hence $\rho\sigma$ fixes every presentation generator of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. [F2, algebra]

Mutual inverses and the zero-sector statement. Both composites fix all generators of their source algebras, so $\rho\sigma=\operatorname{id}$ and $\sigma\rho=\operatorname{id}$; in particular the maps are algebra isomorphisms, and on idempotents they are the literal identity. If $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ then the already constructed $\sigma$ would satisfy $\sigma(e_\alpha)=1_R$ with $e_\alpha=0$, forcing $1_R=0$; conversely the forward identities force $H^\Lambda_\alpha=0$ if $R^\Lambda_\alpha=0$. Zero rings and rank zero are therefore included without any nonzero-block premise. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

Conclusion. Summing the isomorphisms over the finite set of height-$d$ contents and using that the $e_\alpha$ are central orthogonal idempotents summing to $1$ by [F3] gives $H^\Lambda_d\cong\bigoplus_\alpha R^\Lambda_\alpha$. Neither exact dimension nor primitive terminology has entered the proof; the full colour-case verifications, affine six-coefficient calculation and equal-colour divided-difference computation reside in the normalization supplier and the two preceding local relation lemmas. No choice principle and no algebraic closure are used. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎
